posts.author: AphoticAmaranth
posts.body:
RPG Maker is slowly dying. Official support for MV has since been discontinued, and it kinda got enshittified. Meanwhile, the newer RPG Makers, Unite and U2U, aren't exactly looking very promising. As a result, a couple of people I know, myself included, have been gradually moving on to other engines for a while now, and thus have less of a reason to be as active as before, or even remain here.
AI could also be a factor. Even with rules against AI in place, the fact that people still post AI slop resources/plugins, or try to advocate for AI in threads where it is irrelevant, is a blight unto this forum. Which makes it unpleasant for humans who just want to get away from that crap, and buries or derails noteworthy topics.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
AphoticAmaranth said:
Official support for MV has since been discontinued
Click to expand...
But what about MZ? lol
I think your point still stands is likely the most contributing factor:
Without any new RM engines, especially notable engines with a presence here on RMW, the only people using the site are those still building their games in the legacy engines. Over time, that's going to dwindle since the ratio new users entering to old users departing is depreciating.
I'd say AI is also a factor too, likely what SG said. People have gotten scared of interacting with people and/or find the faster, more immediate response of a chatbot better for their workflow. Chatbots unfortunately remove a lot of necessary friction, so it's no wonder a lot of people gravitate towards that than to post on the forum, wait 24 hours for a reply that may or may not be helpful and in rare cases may even be insulting.
Finally, while probably only a small contributing factor to overall community health, a lack of frequent events likely harms retention. I does seem like the mods are hoping to remedy that fact this year, since HiddenOne asked earlier this year what events we'd like to see, but considering there was quite a drought of regular events before, that likely harmed some retention.
I'd also like to argue that Discord is probably not as big of a contributing factor as you might think, since both can coexist at the same time. I have Discord open and RMW open all the time, lol.
The problem with Discord is that all the help has been locked to chats in servers that cannot be search in Google results. This gives RMW a leg up that likely brings many members to the site. They google a problem, they find the result here. They join to ask follow up questions to thank the person for their support (it's likely necroing, but we're glad to have them)
It's also for this reason we often ask people to share their solution if they end up finding on their own, and locking threads when the solution has been found.

posts.author: Anastasius
posts.body:
The proximate cause is AI but it's much more than that. I also doubt RPG Maker and its communities in aggregate are dying.
Last time I remember, on weekends there were something like 100+ guys logged in at any one time and 3K to 5K guests. I don't think Discord can account for those thousands that have since left.
Why are you guys surprised people left the forums? Even before AI, people came here simply for tech or resource support. They were never here to make friends or interact with the community. If you look at the support threads during our site's heyday, most of the questions were really "dumb" or "lazy" that a few of our most active members were more than happy to snark about judging by the number of laughing emojis those snarky posts garnered. People complained about it here and elsewhere. But at that time the forums have had a monopoly on answers so the attitude the powers that be here adopted was "It's our way or the highway."
Is it really surprising people flocked to AI? AI removed a lot of "unnecessary" friction. The forums can rightfully claim AI merely swiped most of their answers from here. But would the average user of RPG Maker really care? AI is doing right now what the forums had always been providing: answers. And unlike our forum helpers who are real human beings with human frailties, AI is a certified bootlicker who will flatter one's ego all day long, hallucinations be damned.
Is the community dying? I doubt it. Case it point, the much-derided RPG Maker subreddit. A year ago the number of weekly visitors there was 42K, a few weeks ago it was 43K, then as of posting it's 44K. Let's be frank, the subreddit (and reddit general) is a mess. Unlike our beautifully organized forum subsections, it's really hard to find useful stuff in the subreddit. It's more like a stream-of-consciousness thing with people weaponizing the downvoting system. But the numbers are thriving. The difference I can think of is that people don't go to the subreddit because they have to, but because they want to. So it actually got bigger in the age of AI. (To be fair, it had a LOT of AI slop and still does.) There's also the fact that the subreddit's most active members are heterogenous in their worldviews. In our forums the most active members are largely a homogenous bunch.
As for the engine itself RPG Maker's target market has always been the Japanese market; RPG Maker was never even meant for export until a bunch of guys pirated it. As long as they keep making Harold games in Japan RPG Maker would always make money and so it will still be around for a while.
Are our forums a lost cause? No. It's adapting but unfortunately it doesn't too its own horn. Case in point, it's no longer as snarky as before. The one answering most of the support threads is now Robro33 and to a lesser extent rpgLord69 and SolarFlare. Looking at the posts of these guys, especially Robro33, I hardly saw any post where they had been patronizing towards an OP who asked "dumb" or "lazy" questions.
Our forums currently have an identity crisis. What does it want to be going forward?
Should it be where you get answers that AI can't provide? Answers which AI will immediately swipe.
Should it be like a Discord channel that's closed to AI parsers?
Should it be a wild saloon like the RPG Maker subreddit where all comers are welcome, just beware of flying bottles, chairs, and guys?
Should it revolve around the 20 most active members, guest numbers going down to zero be damned?

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
Anastasius said:

I think this is an interesting point, but even if you don't want to be part of the community, if you come to a forum, you are interacting with humans, if you are to interact e.g. by asking questions. Which means just talking to people how you would want to be approached and considering of the other party.
While I cannot speak for all members, for me there is a certain frustration with the people who tend to use the forum like a search bar: writing a single sentence and wait for people to cater them with follow up questions or tons of options since there is no way to help them out without either putting a lot of time into the answer (by giving all possible answers to the question) or by putting the time in pulling the information out of the requester to be able to answer precisely.
And then, if an answer is provided don't bother to show any gratitude towards the people helping them or express wheather their problem was solved.
I have a long list of people who I don't help anymore because they frustrate me. I don't publically announce that I think x,y and z are *redacted*s, but for example if I did an extensive list of options as an answer to a post to help someone out and they never bothered to tell me if that solved the problem, I'm not doing it again for them. You could say, I am not entitled to a kind answer, but neither are they to my time.
On the other hand, if someone shows up and their first post is properly formulated and allows you to help without having to do several rounds of feedback loop (not because they are clearly a beginner, but obviously too lazy) and they seem nice enough (or... just communicate normally how you'd communicate with humans you ask for a little favor), there is no reason to not help without any fuss - if I can in a reasonable amount of my own time.
While it is certainly not recommended to crash out on people, it can really get you. And not everyone will act ideal, everyone here is a human, and given we are the people using RM, there is a pretty high rate of people who are a little different. It is, what it is.
And after all, if you want a place where you can go and ask people questions, you need to make it in a way that they don't get annoyed and stop doing so - if you want that option to keep existing.
A while ago I did a stroll on reddit, after someone announced that everyone here is a *redacted* and reddit is so much nicer and they'll just be there.
It was really interesting, since most of the resource requests there I could have easily answered... and most just weren't. Probably part of the structure there, but also part to it just not being the place where the people knowing these things lurk. If there were answers, there were often not really solving the issue or pointing at packs on itch that often would not fit in style. Did not make a full analysis though, so maybe some are solved properly - but just at that glance I didn't find any that had a really helpful answer or godforbid someone creating something to help.
Funnily, to cross check, I looked at reddit and found this:
Which is unanswered since two days, while here in the forum, it is long solved:
MV - Looking for more character generation hairstyles/outfits
I've been trying to make a character with pigtails using the generator but the only one that is somewhat close uses flowers in the hair. I only need them removed for the walking sprite so does anyone know of any assets, DLC, or places I can find more hair styles/other generator options?  I...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
At a point where OP had only two posts and was clearly not an established member. But! They were also not acting like an entitled prick and mysteriously that yielded success.
A little addition: Any request here is literally asking strangers for their time and/or knowledge. And if you are not disregarding that and act like you approach a search bar or vending machine (that operates without cash), but just as a person or collective you don't know but wish to get a hand from, you are good.

posts.author: sabao
posts.body:
This could be a totally ignorant take, as I'm only ever around here in short bursts every 2-3 years, but I think RMW enjoyed a lot of the traffic it had at its peak because it was the official publisher of the RPG Maker series for a while.
It feels to me like GGG dropped the ball with their latest product
and
community management, so the user base fragmented into smaller micro communities instead of congregating into a single forum like this one. To RMW's credit, there was a strong effort to build community. Before RMXP (Oh, my knees) there would have been like 6 or 7 big RM-centric forums and half of them probably didn't like each other.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
If you look at the stats at the bottom of the screen, part of the reason is because after AI the visitors jumped from one thousand to ten thousand (before the bots were limited). Also it used to show members online an hour after they had already left, now it updates much faster it seems.
Discords took away lots of users, AI took away even more. Losing publisher status affected traffic. AquaEcho marketed other engines so much that people left to use them. A lot of people were also coming here for the snarky replies, like visiting a tsundere maid-cafe.
I would guess a big reason is also that people here get very little engagement for their games (used to be like that already in 2021 when I joined, but now it's even less). I think there's 3 people here at the moment who sometimes play or comment other rpgmaker games. And even the few small streamers have left or quit streaming.

posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
Part of the issue I've found with "engagement for their games" is that when you try to get that here... You're asking peole who are amateurs at building games to give you technical feedback on your game.
I tried at one point to offer advice for "how to make your game more fun", but those posts usually start arguments or end in hurt feelings, because nobody wants to admit "Yeah, my game has some problems and it isn't fun".
I critisized the color palette of one section of a game before (a user was angry he got some negative feedback on his game that someone on YouTube did during a stream) and wanted to vent here.  I went looking for the "hateful comments" in that stream, found basically a lot of nothing burgers (basically people saying the game itself wasn't good, no personal attacks or anything), and then tried to offer my own perspective.  My own feedback of the color palette was "looking at this section of game is like Kryptonite to people who aren't color blind.  I suggest you learn some color theory and maybe rework this, because it is ROUGH on the eyes".
Cue 14 post argument with them about "The game just isn't for you.  I didn't design it for you." and "You're wrong" and "you're just a hater".
BTW, the argument of "I didn't design this for you" tells anyone with a brain that you have no idea how to design a game in the first place.  You didn't design an RPG, my favorite genre of video game, for me?  Who did you design it for?  Majong players?
Listen, I'LL tell YOU if the game is "not something for me".  But, if you're advertising "This is an RPG" and when I play it, it is some of the most incompetently designed RPG mechanics, characters, writing, and story I've ever run across... You have most definitely designed this game for me.  You're just REALLY BAD at designing this game for me.
If you're advertising a platformer though, and I play it.  I'll go, "I am not generally into platformers, but here's my impressions just in case you find them useful.".  I will acknowledge your game is "not for me" right from the jump.
I don't pick up Street Fighter games because I am not a Fighting Game guy.  But, if asked for feedback on them, I'll give you my (probably highly uninformed) opinion on them.
I ain't into Dragon Warrior, either.  I prefer the spin off games to the series as they are a lot more fun.  I don't play them, they ain't for me.  So, I can only give my impression (highly uninformed as it may be) on them.
Anyway, back on topic.
I decided a few years ago to just stop offering feedback for games in these forums because it was almost universally met with "it's just not for you" or some other form of "The GameDev can't handle feedback and learn".  I don't think I'm the only one who is like this, either.
Why bother offering feedback and engagement for the other users, if there's a pretty good chance that they're just going to argue with you?  Or make up excuses not to fix things?  This is most likely a bridge burned by inexperienced and young users.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body: Yeah, but there's different kinds of engagement and feedback. Many hobbyist just want someone to acknowledge that they played their game and say something "nice" about it. There's this thought bias here that people want proper feedback like for a commercial game.

posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
They should just be up front about that.  "Hey, will someone play my game and say something nice about it?".
I'm not sure how useful that is to making a game, but it's at least what the user wants.  I can find good things about bad games (I play a LOT of bad games and get enjoyment out of them), and it would drastically shorten how long we'd need to play a game before being able to put it down.

All i'll say I'm technically in about of 10 different RPG Maker related Discord Servers plus some other Game Dev related Discord Servers, plus the subreddit and RPG Maker.net which is now back online, and I've heard there's more scattered about lol.
Most of the 'action' seems to be in the subreddit and the discord servers from my experience.
Plus, if your into older RPG Makers, it seems your going to get more help in the discord servers or subreddit, especially since if you ask about stuff like maniacs patch here, you'll be pointed elsewhere, which is fair enough, and they are the minority of users, but that is a group of users that have been driven away from these forums and ofc you have the fan game communities and pokemon essentials community which understandably will go to subreddit, discords and RPMN instead of here.
